title: Microsoft Entra: sensitivity labels for cloud security groups
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, opt-in setting, controls and preview limitations are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. Add the general licensing reference that explicitly identifies manual sensitivity labeling as included in Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Apply sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups to extend the classification and governance you already use for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap says no separate label configuration is required.
claims.quote: The same labels you publish in the Microsoft Purview portal and configure for groups and sites apply automatically to cloud security groups, with no separate label configuration required.

claims.claim: Cloud security groups use the same published labels configured for groups and sites.
claims.quote: The same labels you publish in the Microsoft Purview portal and configure for groups and sites apply automatically to cloud security groups, with no separate label configuration required.

claims.claim: The capability extends label-based protection already available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

claims.claim: Labels enforce membership policies when groups are created or labelled.
claims.quote: automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can enforce guest access restrictions on cloud security groups.
claims.quote: If the selected label includes a policy that blocks guest access, you can't add guest members.

claims.quote: Labels can be assigned through the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell, or Microsoft Graph.

claims.quote: Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.

claims.claim: No action is required to receive the change.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An assigned cloud security group label cannot currently be changed or removed.
claims.quote: During preview, you can't change sensitivity labels on cloud security groups. After you apply a label, you can't modify or remove it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in: it requires tenant enablement before it can restrict security groups.
claims.quote: To apply sensitivity labels to cloud security groups, you must enable the feature by creating or updating tenant-level directory settings.

claims.claim: Cloud security groups use the tenant-level Group.Security template, separate from Group.Unified.
claims.quote: Cloud security groups use the `Group.Security` settings template, which is separate from the `Group.Unified` template used for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: EnableMIPLabels must be True for cloud security groups in tenant directory settings.
claims.quote: The `EnableMIPLabels` setting is set to `True` for cloud security groups in your tenant directory settings.

claims.claim: New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params enables support using the specified template and EnableMIPLabels value.
claims.quote:
templateId = "d209f6fa-3839-4d70-b83f-60b1c64d0e8f"
name = "EnableMIPLabels"
value = "True"
New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Existing Group.Security settings are updated with Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting.
claims.quote:
If the settings already exist and you need to update them:
Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $Setting.Id `
    -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: No admin centre toggle for enabling cloud security group sensitivity labels is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "sensitivity labels" "admin" "enable". Read groups-sensitivity-labels in full and search excerpts for container enablement; these document directory-settings PowerShell, not a tenant UI toggle.

claims.claim: Existing group labels are assigned in Microsoft Entra ID > Groups > All groups > group > Properties > Sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Select Microsoft Entra ID. Select Groups > All groups, and then select the group you want to label. On the group's page, select Properties. Select a sensitivity label from the Sensitivity label dropdown.

claims.claim: The new-group entry point is Groups > All groups > New group.
claims.quote: Select Groups > All groups > New group.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/groups/{id} can assign a sensitivity label through assignedLabels.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups/0d09007d-45b2-458c-b180-880dde3a302e
assignedLabels: The list of sensitivity label pairs (label ID, label name) associated with a Microsoft 365 group or a cloud security group.

claims.claim: Group.ManageProtection.All delegated permission is documented for setting assignedLabels on cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Group.ManageProtection.All delegated permission is the least privileged permission to update the assignedLabels property for cloud security groups.

claims.claim: App-only assignment of cloud security group labels is unsupported.
claims.quote: Group.ManageProtection.All delegated permission is the least privileged permission to update this property for cloud security groups. App-only scenarios aren't supported.

claims.claim: The person assigning a label must be the group owner or at least a Groups Administrator.
claims.quote: The current signed-in user has sufficient privileges to assign sensitivity labels (group owner or at least a Groups Administrator)

claims.claim: The assigning user must be within the label publishing policy's scope.
claims.quote: and is within the scope of the sensitivity label publishing policy.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync starts sensitivity label synchronization into Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Use the Execute-AzureADLabelSync cmdlet to start the synchronization of sensitivity labels into Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync must run in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not the Microsoft Graph SDK.
claims.quote: The `Execute-AzureADLabelSync` cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available.
claims.quote: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available.

claims.claim: An admin UI for initiating label synchronization is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Execute-AzureADLabelSync" "portal" synchronization. Read the cmdlet and feature pages and the container synchronization search excerpt; the documented initiation is Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Labels must be published in Microsoft Purview with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are published in the Microsoft Purview portal with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are managed in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled <$true|$false> is a documented general label control.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the sensitivity label that you want to modify.
The SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter enables or disables the Site and Group Protection action for the label.

claims.claim: The pages read do not identify which Set-Label parameters apply specifically to cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "Set-Label". Read the feature page and searched the Set-Label reference for security group applicability; neither enumerates cloud-security-group-specific parameter support.

claims.claim: No UI or API for changing or removing an assigned cloud security group label is documented during preview.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "sensitivity labels" "change" "remove" Graph. Read groups-sensitivity-labels and group-update; both state assigned labels are immutable, and no changing/removal operation is documented.

claims.claim: Learn's workaround for the wrong label is a new security group with the correct label and re-added members.
claims.quote: To change a label, create a new security group with the correct label, and then re-add the members to the new group.

claims.claim: Security groups are authorization primitives used in Conditional Access scoping, application access and resource permissions.
claims.quote: Security groups are used directly in authorization decisions such as Conditional Access scoping, application access, and resource permissions.

claims.claim: Enforcement depends on Microsoft Entra ID membership resolution and validation.
claims.quote: Enforcement depends on Microsoft Entra ID's membership resolution and validation logic, not on administrative governance practices alone.

claims.claim: Listed roles, including Global Administrator, User Administrator and Groups Administrator, can bypass policies when adding members.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are unsupported on dynamic-membership security groups in this release.
claims.quote: You can't apply sensitivity labels to security groups with dynamic membership in this release.

claims.claim: Edge cases can allow a label on a dynamic group without enforcing its policy.
claims.quote: While there are certain edge cases where you can apply a label to a dynamic group, the associated label policy isn't enforced.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Nested groups must be removed before labelling a parent security group.
claims.quote: You can't label a group that currently contains nested groups. To label a parent group, remove all nested (child) groups first, apply the label to the parent, and then add the child groups back.

claims.claim: Child groups need labels at least as restrictive as the parent's.
claims.quote: When you add a child group back to a labeled parent, the child group's label must be at least as restrictive as the parent's label.
